title: ACOS evaluates RN53(RN64(pi/2 - ASIN(x))), inheriting ASIN's 1-ULP sign asymmetry
statement: In Excel 16.0 build 20430, ACOS(x) does not satisfy ACOS(-x) = pi - ACOS(x) to the last bit: ACOS(0.5) returns 0x3ff0c152382d7365 (1.0471975511965976) while ACOS(-0.5) returns 0x4000c152382d7366 (2.0943951023931957), and ACOS(0.75) vs ACOS(-0.75) similarly reflect ASIN's asymmetric 1 + x = 2 - (1 - x) staging followed by stored x87 subtraction from pi/2. All 13,962 full-bank ACOS rows match this graph.
basis: Measured across paired signed controls in CalcFunc-Evidence runs/w111-acos-caller-20260929/answers-acos.json.gz (Excel 16.0 build 20430) and matched on 13,962/13,962 full-bank ACOS witness rows.
inferred: That the stored x87 pi/2 - ASIN(x) decomposition explains every ACOS input beyond the 13,962 bank rows is inferred.
